info.name: Glonez Backend
info.description:
Glonez language training centre — Staff + User endpoints, Neero gateway (with anti-spoof callback re-verification + type/amount cross-check), claims, accounts, transfers, withdrawals, and partial-payment support.

Usage:
1. Import the matching environment (Development, Staging, or Production).
2. Run `Staff › Auth › Login` or `User › Auth › Login` — the test script automatically saves `staffToken` / `userToken` to your environment.
3. All staff/user requests pick up the token via `{{staffToken}}` / `{{userToken}}`.

User accounts: only staff can create users. `phone` is **required** (credentials are SMS'd); `email` is optional (extra copy emailed if present).

Partial payments: `POST /users/payments/initiate` accepts an optional `amount`. If omitted, it defaults to whatever is still owed on the class. The server validates `amount <= remaining` (pending intents count against `remaining`). Use `GET /users/payments/class-summary[/:classId]` (or the staff equivalent `GET /staff/payments/class-summary?userId=&classId=`) to see `{ expected, paid, pending, remaining, fullyPaid, paymentsCount }`.

Dev mode (NODE_ENV != production):
The backend routes payment & withdrawal calls to an in-process simulator, so use `+237670000001` (the value of `{{devTestPhone}}`) as the phone. Send header `x-simulate-outcome: failed` to force a failed outcome (default = success).

Neero callbacks:
One endpoint receives both payment and withdrawal callbacks (`POST /api/public/callbacks/neero`). The server discriminates by the prefix of `externalTransactionId` (`PAY-…` → Payment, `WDR-…` → Withdrawal). PENDING callbacks are acknowledged and ignored. For non-pending callbacks, the server re-queries Neero using the stored `gatewayReference` (the Neero `transactionIntentId`) and additionally cross-checks the returned intent's `type` (must be `CASHIN` for payments, `CASHOUT` for withdrawals) and `amount`. The callback body itself never drives the status update — spoofed payloads are dropped.

Neero payment-method cache:
The server keeps a local `(phoneNumber, provider) → neeroPaymentMethodId` cache so repeat payments and withdrawals skip the extra `POST /payment-methods` round-trip.

Pagination: list endpoints accept `pageNum` (default 1) and `pageSize` (default 10).

Response shape: every endpoint returns HTTP 200 with `{ success, data, errorMsg, errorCode }`. Frontends gate on `success` + `errorCode`.

request.description: Phone is required (credentials are SMS'd). Email is optional — if provided a copy of the credentials is also emailed.
Manager+ only. A disabled user cannot log in; existing sessions return errorCode 2005 (ACCOUNT_DISABLED) on the next authenticated request.

Create up to 500 users in one call.

- Per-row: `name` and `phone` required; `email` and `classId` optional.
- `options.skipDuplicates` (default `true`): a row whose phone or email already exists is moved to `skipped` rather than failing the row.
- Returns `{ summary, created, skipped, failed }`. Each list carries the original row `index` so the UI can map outcomes back to its grid.
- Credentials are SMS'd to every created user (email copy when provided). One transport failing does not roll back the user record.

request.description: Admin only. `isActive` is NOT accepted here — use the dedicated /disable and /enable endpoints below so the role-hierarchy guard is always applied.

Open to any authenticated staff, but enforces role hierarchy:
- You cannot disable yourself (`cannot_disable_self`, 1003).
- You cannot disable an admin (`cannot_disable_admin`, 1003).
- Your role must be STRICTLY GREATER than the target's (`cannot_disable_higher_role`, 1003).

So a manager (600) can disable an auditor (500) or support (200); only admin can disable a manager.
Same role-hierarchy rules as Disable — re-enabling an auditor requires manager+ for example.
Pay only part of the class fee. Server validates amount <= remaining (pending intents count against remaining). Omit `amount` to default to the full remaining balance.
